header_sentences: See Cause, Honour, Gain, Reputation, etc.

contexts.text: For the sake of his reputation.

To do what is just and fair for the sake of self and the world; that is, for the sake of his own honour or reputation, and for the sake of the wealth and possessions of the world; and also for the sake of the fear of the law.
Regards health of mind... not for the sake of reputation, honours, gain; but for the sake of the life after death.
For these had done good for the sake of good, or for the sake of truth; and had done what is just for the sake of what is just, or fair; not for the sake of gain, honour, and the like.
Perceives delight in doing well to the neighbour for the sake of truth and good; and not for the sake of self or the world.
Mutual love without an end for the sake of self and for the sake of the world.
For these have not the affection of truth for the sake of truth, still less for the sake of life; but for the sake of gain...
But those who are in the affection of truth for the sake of truth, and for the sake of life, consequently, for the sake of the Lord's Kingdom...
Those who learn truths not for the sake of truth, nor for the sake of life, but for the sake of gain...
The Spiritual... is the affection of good and truth for the sake of good and truth, and not for the sake of self...
(The Angels have no latent thought of) wishing well to the neighbour for the sake of themselves.
Celestial love is quite averse to doing well to anyone for the sake of self; but it does it for the sake of the good which is with the other... consequently for the sake of the Lord Himself...
He who had learned the truths of faith, not for the sake of willing and doing them... but only for the sake of knowing, and teaching them, for the sake of honour and gain...
This illustration (is) in such as long to know truths, not for the sake of reputation and glory, but for the sake of life and use. AC 10551:2.
If they do good, it is for the sake of self.

Everyone may provide (wealth and honours) for himself; not for the sake of self, but for the sake of the neighbour. He who does so for the sake of self, provides evilly for himself; but he who does so for the sake of the neighbour, provides well for himself.
For the sake of the lust of exercising command, and of gain, they confess (truths and goods of faith).

All perceive delight (there) in doing evil, who (here) do not do well to the neighbour for the sake of the neighbour, nor to their country for the sake of their country, nor to the Church for the sake of the Church; but for the sake of self: consequently, who do not do truth and good for the sake of truth and good.
Faith (is to want to know what is true and good), not for the sake of doctrine as the end, but for the sake of life.

Spiritual good is... not for the sake of gain, nor for the sake of honour; but for the sake of the Church, and for the sake of the salvation of the neighbour... Those in the externals of the Church (are) affected with truths of faith principally for the sake of self, and secondarily for the sake of the Church.

Those who act from affection... do truth for the sake of truth, and good for the sake of good, and thus exercise charity for the sake of the neighbour. (Otherwise those who act from obedience. Explained.)
They who do truth for the sake of truth, do it for the sake of the Lord... To do truth for the sake of truth, is to do good.

Signs that sins have been remitted. - They perceive delight in worshipping God for the sake of God, in serving the neighbour for the sake of the neighbour; thus in doing good for the sake of good, and in believing truth for the sake of truth.
And to act for the sake of self is to act for the sake of gain, honours, and reputation, as ends; and not for the sake of the salvation of the neighbour and the Lord's glory.
All who will and do good and truth for the sake of good and truth. Signified, Explained.
To love the neighbour for the sake of self, is [to do so] for the sake of gain and honour as the ends.
Under Truth, see this reference. AC 10683:2. AC 10683:3. AC 10683:4. AC 10683:5.
Those who have Heaven in them... perceive delight in doing well to others, not for the sake of self and the world, but for the sake of good and truth... (The contrary state ex.)
That (hypocrites) do well, is for the sake of self; if it is for the sake of others, it is that they may be seen, and is thus also for the sake of self.
Heavenly love is to love uses for the sake of uses, or goods for the sake of goods...
The love of dignities and riches for the sake of themselves; and for the sake of uses. Explained.
A judge is for the sake of justice; a magistrate for the sake of the common weal; and a king for the sake of the kingdom; and not the reverse.

(He then thinks) that the commonwealth is for the sake of him, and not he for the sake of (it)... Like a king who thinks that the kingdom and all its men are for the sake of him; and not he for the sake of (them).
They prayed to God the Father for the sake of the Son.
For My name's sake hast laboured () = the acknowledgement of the Lord... Explained, Illustrated.
See Good.
For the sake of the Son. AE 114:3. AE 805:4, Explained.
That good is to be done... for the sake of good; and not for the sake of self and the world. Signified.
To receive truth for the sake of truth. Signified.
When man abstains from evils... for the sake of civil laws...
On account of this () = because they are such.
